paper_title: Recent Progress on New Charge Transfer Pathways in Organic Solar Cells

knowledge_points.content: The fundamental difference between traditional donor-acceptor (D-A) devices and Z-type devices lies in how they combine energy from active layers: D-A devices superimpose currents, whereas Z-type devices superimpose voltages.
knowledge_points.evidence: In D-A device, the currents from both layers are superimposed, while in Z-type device, the voltages from the two light-active layers are superimposed.

knowledge_points.content: A bilayer organic solar cell mimicking natural photosynthesis using chlorophyll derivatives (Chl-A and Chl-D) achieved a maximum power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 1.3%.
knowledge_points.evidence: A bilayer device was successfully fabricated to mimic the Z-scheme process of oxygenic photosynthesis, which achieved a maximum efficiency of 1.3%.

knowledge_points.content: The red shift observed in the absorption spectra of chlorophyll thin films prepared by spin-coating is attributed to J-aggregation of the molecules.
knowledge_points.evidence: Compared with the monomeric material in tetrahydrofuran (THF) solution, the red shift observed in the absorption spectra (Figure 2c) of the Chl thin film prepared by spin-coating is attributed to J-aggregation.

knowledge_points.content: Incorporating a $TiO_2$-Chl-C sensitized layer as an electron extraction layer in a trilayer biosolar cell increased the short-circuit current density ($J_{SC}$) to 10.66 $mA/cm^2$ and the PCE to 4.14%.
knowledge_points.evidence: The addition of 1% Chl-C2 to the mixture results in a significant increase in $J_{SC}$ from 9.34 to 10.66 $m	ext{Acm}^{-2}$... leading to a higher PCE of 4.14% (Figure 3f).

knowledge_points.content: Using a Z-type bilayer hole transport layer (HTL) composed of Chl-A and $H_2$-Chl in perovskite solar cells resulted in a power conversion efficiency of 14.1%.
knowledge_points.evidence: Compared with monolayer Chl-based PSCs, this approach exhibits enhanced stability and achieved a higher PCE of 14.1% (Figure 4c).

knowledge_points.content: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis of the $Chl-A/C_{60}$ interface shows that electrons flow from Chl-A toward $C_{60}$, creating an electric dipole layer that establishes an intrinsic electric field.
knowledge_points.evidence: By analyzing the change of the binding energy of inner-shell electrons in Chl-A upon deposition of $C_{60}$ they found that the electrons in Chl-A flow toward the $C_{60}$, forming an electric dipole layer pointing from Chl-A toward $C_{60}$.

knowledge_points.content: In Z-type devices, the open-circuit voltage ($V_{OC}$) is determined by the difference between the quasi-Fermi level of the electrons in one active material (e.g., Chl-A) and the quasi-Fermi level of the holes in the other (e.g., $C_{60}$).
knowledge_points.evidence: It is known that the $V_{OC}$ is determined by the difference between the quasi-Fermi level of the electrons in Chl-A and that of the holes in $C_{60}$ when the heterojunction formed a complete circuit with an external circuit... $V_{OC} = E^n_{F-Chl-A} - E^p_{F-C60}$

knowledge_points.content: Treating Chl-A films with ethylenediamine (EDA) reduces its work function from 4.73 eV to 4.65 eV, which enhances the built-in electric field at the interface and increases device efficiency by 280%.
knowledge_points.evidence: the treatment of EDA results in a decrease in the work function of Chl-A from 4.73 to 4.65 eV... the overall efficiency of the device increases by 280%

knowledge_points.content: The Z-type charge transfer characteristic is experimentally observed in IPCE measurements when the maximum charge generation efficiency occurs at the overlap of the absorption spectra of the two photoactive materials.
knowledge_points.evidence: in the IPCE test of the Z-characteristic device, the efficiency of charge generation would be highest when there is a greatest overlap of the absorption spectra of two photoactive materials.

knowledge_points.content: The 'small injection hypothesis' in organic semiconductors is limited because their low equilibrium carrier concentration means photogenerated nonequilibrium carriers significantly influence the built-in electric field.
knowledge_points.evidence: the applicability of small injection assumption is limited for organic semiconductors. It is mainly because organic semiconductors have a lower equilibrium carrier concentration than inorganic semiconductors, and light-generated nonequilibrium carriers cause a significant influence to the equilibrium carriers.

knowledge_points.content: In Z-type devices, the recombination of photogenerated holes from one layer and photogenerated electrons from the other at the interface serves as the primary current generator, whereas in D-A devices, this process is considered leakage current.
knowledge_points.evidence: In the operation of D-A type devices, $I_1$ plays a crucial role in generating the main current... while $I_2$ serves as the leakage current. On the other hand, in the operation of Z-type devices, $I_1$ acts as the leakage current, while $I_2$ [electron movement from lower LUMO to higher HOMO] becomes the primary current generator.

knowledge_points.content: The interconnecting layer (ICL) in tandem organic solar cells facilitates a Z-type charge transfer process to connect the subcells.
knowledge_points.evidence: In tandem devices, two subcells are usually composed of traditional D-A structured OSCs. And their ICL forms the Z-type CT.
